scope: Manual review of all twelve remaining p2816 interfaces against the pinned library and frozen finite-dimensional source conventions.

rows.query: Search design-dependent conditional noise and inspect Borel probability kernels and joint kernel measure construction.
rows.result: A probability kernel from the latent design input to the noise vector represents the conditional law, while its moment constraints are additional properties.
rows.gap: The conditional-noise model still needs the almost-everywhere zero-mean and directional second-moment constraints on its probability kernel.

comparisons.D3: Take nu as a Borel probability kernel Xi to R^n, indexed by the latent xi, with the referenced D4/D5 conditions. Noise may depend on xi and have correlated coordinates; neither Gaussianity, independence from the operator nor iid coordinate sampling follows. Regular conditional probability means a measurable law of noise at xi, not a fixed marginal law or merely an a.e. conditional expectation.

rows.query: Search random linear operators and finite matrix measurability; inspect matrix-as-indexed-array and its finite linear action.
rows.result: Finite matrices represent the operator, with measurability of coordinate functionals supporting the measurable matrix-valued observation.
rows.gap: The random-operator model still needs its measurable Xi-indexed matrix map and probability law, without imposing additional moment or rank restrictions.

comparisons.D2: n,d are positive finite integers; each matrix coordinate is a linear functional, so finite-dimensional coordinate measurability gives the usual Borel matrix map once the spaces are set. No finite E||T||^2, full column rank, Gaussian design or iid rows is assumed. xi indexes the operator but is not itself necessarily observed; estimators only receive T_xi and y.

rows.query: Search conditional covariance bounds and inspect directional second-moment integral and positive-semidefinite quadratic form.
rows.result: Directional quadratic integrals can state the bound, and PSD order can encode a matrix version after proving integrability and a common full-measure set.
rows.gap: The conditional covariance bound still needs finite moments and a justified passage from fixed-direction almost-everywhere bounds to any simultaneous matrix inequality.

comparisons.D5: For each fixed u integrate (u-transpose w)^2 against nu(.|xi), bounded above by u-transpose Sigma_w u for P-a.e. xi. With D4 this is covariance control, not covariance equality or only a marginal bound. Coordinate directions give finite second moments; a countable dense set can support a common null-set argument in finite dimensions, but it is not silently part of the printed quantifier. The bound does not assert invertibility of Sigma_w.

rows.query: Inspect vector Bochner integral and conditional zero-mean semantics, including nonintegrability fallback.
rows.result: The vector integral at each conditional law expresses the source condition once integrability is established.
rows.gap: Conditional mean zero still requires an integrable noise vector under almost every conditional law.

comparisons.D4: Require integral w under nu(dw|xi)=0 for P-a.e. xi, not just E w=0 and not conditional on y. Alone the total Bochner integral equals zero for nonintegrable functions, so genuine mean existence must accompany the equation; the finite-dimensional second-moment bound D5 supplies a route to it. Do not infer conditional symmetry, Gaussianity or independence from zero mean.

rows.query: Search moment-constrained conditional noise classes and inspect normalized kernel and moment definitions.
rows.result: A class of probability kernels with two a.e. moment constraints can be stated, without reducing it to a parametric Gaussian family.
rows.gap: The admissible-noise class still needs the conjunction of the precise conditional mean and covariance-bound conditions relative to P.

comparisons.D6: Membership in P(Sigma_w) concerns the conditional kernel nu indexed by xi, with D4 and D5 holding P-almost everywhere. It is not a class of fixed R^n laws independent of xi, nor a requirement of covariance exactly Sigma_w. Preserve the dependence on the design-input probability law and finite-moment meaning; this class is optimized adversarially in the minimax risk.

rows.query: Search observed random linear model and inspect matrix action, conditional joint law and measurable pushforward.
rows.result: The conditional joint law can be pushed forward by (xi,w) to (T_xi,T_xi theta-star+w), representing the actual observations.
rows.gap: The observation model still needs its measurable pushforward with only the operator and response exposed to the estimator.

comparisons.D1: theta-star is an unknown fixed parameter; T_xi and y are observed, w is not. Map the joint latent design/noise law through the stated linear equation, using finite matrix action in the main setting. Do not expose extra latent information from xi, assume full-rank T or replace the conditional noise by an independent product distribution. The broader operator wording does not establish infinite-dimensional matrix-inverse formulas.

rows.query: Inspect measure composition-product definition and compare the source's explicit sequential law P times nu.
rows.result: Measure.compProd is exactly the joint law obtained by drawing xi under P and noise from nu conditional on xi.
rows.gap: The specified joint design-noise law is directly represented by the measure composition-product of P and the Markov kernel nu.

comparisons.D7: P compProd nu retains both coordinates and yields conditional integration first over w at fixed xi, then over xi. Probability P and a probability kernel meet the construction's finiteness requirements. The printed multiplication sign is not an independence assertion or the ordinary product with one fixed noise law; the response is a subsequent measurable function of this pair and theta-star.

rows.query: Search measurable deterministic estimator classes and inspect deterministic Dirac kernels against the observed-data domain.
rows.result: Each measurable estimator can be embedded as a deterministic decision kernel, but this does not identify it with the entire randomized estimator class.
rows.gap: The estimator domain still needs to be restricted to measurable functions of the observed matrix and response.

comparisons.D10: The input is (T_xi,y), output is any R^d vector, with no requirement to lie in the constraint ellipse. A deterministic kernel embeds such a function; allowing all Markov kernels would additionally allow randomization. Do not restrict the class to linear/ridge estimators used for the upper proof or let it observe xi beyond T_xi.

rows.query: Search weighted quadratic norms and inspect positive-definite matrix form and inverse identity.
rows.result: Positive-definite quadratic forms represent the two squared norms, with inverse algebra valid after proving the determinant condition.
rows.gap: The norm construction still needs the positive-definite quadratic-form bridge and the inverse constraint metric kept distinct from the error metric.

comparisons.D8: Use theta-transpose K_e theta for squared error geometry and theta-transpose K_c^-1 theta for constraint geometry, with both K_e and K_c explicitly symmetric positive definite. PosDef is stated on finitely supported vectors, which match finite-dimensional vectors after conversion. Prove the inverse is the intended nonsingular inverse and positive definite; no commutation or simultaneous diagonalization of the two matrices is assumed.

rows.query: Search inverse-information trace risk functional and inspect SPD matrices, functional-calculus powers, inverse hypotheses, trace and supremum/integral domains.
rows.result: The matrix operations and expectation/supremum are available primitives, but they do not supply missing covariance invertibility or endpoint conventions.
rows.gap: The functional still needs invertible noise covariance, a nonempty strict-positive matrix domain and the correctly ordered expected inverse with its trace budget.

comparisons.D12: Omega is deterministic and strictly positive definite, chosen outside expectation over xi. Preserve K_e half powers on both sides of (Omega^-1+T-transpose Sigma_w^-1 T)^-1 and the K_c inverse-half trace budget <=varrho^2; powers are spectral, not entrywise, and matrices need not commute. Sigma_w is not explicitly invertible in N2, so do not insert a pseudoinverse or rely on Lean's total inverse. At varrho=0 no positive Omega is feasible, and an empty real supremum default is not specified. Attainment is not guaranteed; expected inverse cannot be replaced by inverse of expected information, and no second moment of T is assumed. Under valid SPD noise the inverse is bounded by Omega, giving a route to integrability despite heavy-tailed T.

rows.query: Search ellipsoid constraints and inspect SPD inverse quadratic norm and square-root domain.
rows.result: The ellipsoid is a sublevel set of the inverse-weighted quadratic norm, using the stated radius.
rows.gap: The constraint set still needs the inverse-metric norm and faithful treatment of the source's radius notation and endpoint.

comparisons.D9: Theta is {theta:||theta||_(K_c^-1)<=varrho}; the prose says radius R, while the formula and minimax arguments use varrho, so retain the discrepancy. For nonnegative varrho, the norm inequality is equivalent to quadratic form <=varrho^2 after norm construction; squaring without the sign premise would change a negative-radius set. At zero radius it is {0}, which differs from the empty strictly positive Omega feasible set in D12. Estimator outputs need not belong to Theta.

rows.query: Inspect Decision/Risk minimaxRisk and its randomized estimator infimum; compare robust noise-indexed parameter set and observed-data pushforward.
rows.result: Library minimaxRisk provides extended nonnegative minimax loss for kernel experiments, but its randomized decisions and experiment indexing need a bridge to this deterministic robust risk.
rows.gap: The robust minimax risk still needs its observed-data experiment indexed by both parameter and admissible noise kernel and a justified restriction from randomized to deterministic estimators.

comparisons.D11: Take supremum jointly over fixed theta-star in the ellipse and the whole admissible conditional kernel nu, before averaging xi,w under P compProd nu; neither adversary chooses a new parameter after seeing xi. Observation law is the pushforward to (T_xi,y), and loss uses K_e. minimaxRisk ranges over all Markov-kernel decisions, whereas the paper ranges over measurable functions; an embedding gives only one direction without a derandomization argument. Indexing arbitrary noise kernels also needs measurable experiment structure. Retain potentially infinite nonnegative risk and do not use Bochner/toReal defaults to erase nonintegrable losses or replace the robust class by Gaussian proof reductions.
